speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Nerve Entrapment Syndrome (specifically involving the Great Auricular Nerve or Auriculotemporal Nerve) secondary to post-tympanoplasty scarring or hardware placement.

The combination of shooting pain upon chewing (suggesting trigeminal-glossopharyngeal involvement) and pain with earring pressure (indicating auricular nerve irritation) in a patient with recent ear surgery and a history of chronic otitis media is highly suggestive of neuropathic pain rather than simple infection or graft failure. Given the audiology report shows improved hearing, the graft itself appears functional, pointing towards a neurological complication from the surgical approach or scar tissue formation.
